General position, complex characteristic zero and unproved special degenerations are explicitly bounded.

originality.rationale: The claim classifies the complete reduced singular support of the normal decic model arising from the five (1,1) branch curves of Chen–Lazarsfeld–Moretti, with a specific 5×24, 2×64, 1×324 Milnor basket. Their 2026 Theorem 2.2/§§2.4–2.6 give the covering and contraction incidence but do not state this singularity basket. Artal Bartolo–Cogolludo-Agustín–Libgober 2017 construct a different plane cyclic covering of the genus-two Jacobian, without a normal-decic basket. Weighted Jacobian computations are standard tools, not originality claims. Targeted indexed-record and published-literature searches returned no statement implying this exact projective model classification; priority uncertainty persists.
residual_risks: The local computations are consequences of the source contraction configuration; a previously unpublished or unindexed calculation could contain the same singularity census.
A nearby older source on cyclic coverings was materially read only in relevant sections; not every publication containing these branch curves is indexed.
The weighted semi-quasihomogeneous formula is classical, so originality is the assembled exact basket, not the Milnor formalism.
Other special projections and special Q can have additional collisions; excluded by explicit general-position hypotheses.

value.rationale: The initiating 2026 paper establishes the existence of normal degree-ten models for a genus-two Jacobian, leaving local exceptional geometry of those projective models unresolved. A complete natural census of eight isolated singularities with three distinct local Milnor values, and Euler reconciliation of 572 vanishing cycles, quantifies the singularities created by realizing a smooth abelian surface as a normal hypersurface. This classification is not a generic textbook exercise in computing a Milnor number at an arbitrary point: the nontrivial incidence-to-singularity conversion establishes the precise global basket. It is usable for resolution/deformation and topology questions without requiring a downstream theorem.
